extracted_by: hand, T-0290 — the Democrat read, August 1834
note: Vol. I No. 39, the last of the month. THE FIRST STEAMBOAT IN A CHICAGO MARINE LIST IN THIS CORPUS clears for Michigan City here, eight days after the paper reported a hundred hands on the North Pier. Two claims are new trades for the town — a book and stationery store announced as opening on 26 August, and a clerk advertising himself through the post office — and one is the paper's own imprint, which places the Democrat at the corner of South Water and Clark streets nine months after the only other witness this project has for it. The issue also carries a St. Louis reward advertisement for a man held as a slave; it is extracted for what it is, and its subject is not minted as a person because the notice cuts his name after one letter. Page 3 columns 2 and 3 carry the town; pages 1, 2 and 4 are advertising, national reprint and the town ordinances, all of them woven two columns to a row.

A steamboat entering this port in August 1834 is a claim about the depth over the bar that the harbor editorial of 1834-08-13 (claim c002 there) was hoping for, and it arrives eight days after that editorial. The Westward Ho, the Dart, the Hiram and the Juliet are all repeat callers from the previous fortnight. business.name: Chicago Wholesale and Retail Book & Stationary Store

claims.notes: A BOOKSELLER OPENS IN CHICAGO, DATED 26 AUGUST 1834 — 'Chicago Wholesale and Retail Book & Stationary Store', stock received from Philadelphia and New York, announced as a Store they 'purpose opening', which puts the trade in the town within days of this issue. THE PROPRIETORS ARE LOST with the woven half of the column, and so is the address: the line that should carry it reads 'lue store is in brontese and homeo havel', which is two columns of type on one row and is quoted here exactly as it stands rather than guessed at. THE CLAIM IS THE TRADE AND ITS DATE. A town that supports a stationer is a town with clerks, and the reconstruction's South Water and Lake frontages have had no bookseller on them. THE HOUSE IS RUSSELL & CLIFT, AND THIS ENTRY STILL STANDS APART FROM THEIRS ON PURPOSE (T-0327). This is the FIRST printing of the copartnership notice the firm signs “RUSSELL & CLIFT” a week later: 1834-09-03 page 3 column 3 carries the same heading, the same copy date “Chicago, Aug. 26, 1834”, the same body down to “received from Philadelphia, and others from New York and Boston”, and the two surnames this printing lost with the woven half of the column. The identity is therefore documented rather than guessed. It is NOT joined here, because joining it means declaring that two differently-named gazetteer entries are one firm, and the gazetteer has a declared merge rule for PERSONS only — `identity.json` — and none for firms. That gap is T-0304. Until it closes, this entry keeps the only name its own printing gives, and this note carries the relation.

'OAK WOODS' also settles the supply made in the auction-store street claim of 1834-08-20 (c005 there).

claims.notes: A ST. LOUIS ADVERTISEMENT OFFERING A REWARD FOR A MAN HELD AS A SLAVE, PRINTED IN THIS TOWN'S NEWSPAPER IN AUGUST 1834. It is extracted because it is what the Democrat printed, and because a reconstruction whose standard is that a visitor can tell which parts we made up cannot quietly leave out the parts of the record that are hard to look at. WHAT IT STATES: a man escaped on the 15th instant, described by his speech and his manner; he took a four-year-old horse of about fifteen hands with no shoes; a reward is offered for the return of 'said horse and slave', with a lesser sum without the horse; it is signed Wm. H. Ashley and dated St. Louis, 17 August 1834. THE ADVERTISEMENT IS NOT ABOUT CHICAGO and nothing in it places anybody in this town — Illinois was a free state and this notice is a Missouri owner's, running in a lake-port paper because the escape route ran north. THE ESCAPED MAN'S NAME IS CUT AFTER ONE LETTER ('the name of D') and is NOT supplied. He is not minted as a person: this file will not put a man into a gazetteer under an initial an advertisement gave him.

claims.notes: A CORNER THIS PAPER GIVES AND THIS TRANSCRIPTION CANNOT FINISH: 'corner of' on one line, 'and char' on the next, with the first street lost between them. CLARK IS THE READING for 'char' — it is the cross street of every corner named in this run — and the other half is NOT supplied, so the placement's anchor says plainly that one of the two streets is unread. HUBBARD & CO. ARE PLACED ELSEWHERE IN THE CORPUS ('opposite to Fort Dearborn' in the 1834-07-02 run), so this may be a second store or a second reading, and the claim does not choose. THE CONSIGNMENT ITSELF IS THE OTHER HALF: 150 kegs of eastern nails, assorted sizes, landed in Chicago in August 1834 — the fastenings the balloon frame is made of, arriving by the keg.

claims.notes: THE PAPER PLACES ITSELF, A SECOND TIME AND NINE MONTHS LATER THAN THE FIRST. This project's record for the Chicago Democrat office (data/structures/chicago_democrat_office.json) rests on the first issue of 1833-11-26 and on Andreas; the imprint at the foot of this issue says the paper was still printed at the CORNER OF SOUTH WATER AND CLARK STREETS in August 1834, which is what a second witness is for — it does not move the building, it dates the tenancy. THE IMPRINT ALSO PRICES THE PAPER: an imperial sheet, published every Tuesday, at two dollars fifty in advance (the figure is on line 4459, in the woven half, and is bracketed here rather than quoted). THE COLUMN CARRIES THE TOWN ORDINANCES woven through it line by line, which is why only seven of the fifteen lines in the range belong to this claim.

claims.normalized: House and Land [A]g[en]t. […] [L]OTS purchased and Sold or by comm[ission.] […] Building Lots for sale, in the town a[nd] [School section. …]
claims.notes: ONE IMPRESSION OF THE STANDING LAKE STREET LAND-AGENCY CARD. The Democrat sets this advertisement, word for word the same, in every issue from 1834-05-14 to 1834-10-01 — twenty consecutive weeks, eighteen of which set the line ‘purchased and Sold, or by commi[s]sion’ recognisably (T-1051). The card is identified by its copy and not by its display line: the same trade (‘House and Land Agent’), the same offer of building lots in the town and the School Section, the same houses to let, and the same office on Lake street opposite Dr. Temple's. Four lines of the card survive and the rest of it is gone: the display line, the houses to let and the whole address are not in this column. 3037 ('2%') is quoted where it stands because excluding it would hide the interleave, and the lot count it may be a fragment of is not read from it. THE PROPRIETOR'S NAME IS NOT READ HERE and none is supplied into the quote: the record's ‘W. G. Blanchard’ stands on T-0408's reading of the two impressions whose columns are NOT Tesseract fallbacks (1834-07-16 line 5527, 1834-09-17 line 3292) and on identity.json's declared firm merge, not on this impression. This printing is recorded as silent about placement.
